newsitem.title: UK: SR Gent shares gain after Prospero offer.
newsitem.headline: SR Gent shares gain after Prospero offer.

text.p: Shares in Britain's SR Gent Plc, one of the top suppliers of clothing to top retailer Marks & Spencer Plc, rose on Tuesday as privately-owned Prospero Investments said it made an agreed bid for the company.
The 82p per share bid valued the whole of Gent at 30.6 million stg and Gent shares rose 8p at 79-1/2 by 0706 GMT in volume of 10,000 shares.

Prospero said it saw Gent, which warned last September that it was in talks on a refinancing with its banks and that its results would be hit by a write-down of stock, as a business with "significant potential".

Holders of 61.3 percent of Gent shares have already agreed to accept the offer. "After a period of great uncertainty, the offer by Prospero represents a fair value for SR Gent," said chief executive Mike Stakol.
"Going forward, the company will have a new owner committed to textile manufacture and who values the skills and technical ability of our workforce."

Prospero, a specially-formed investment vehicle controlled by family interests of Indonesian businessman Marimutu Sinivasan, said it believed Gent's financial performance would be improved by more efficient manufacturing and stock controls processes.

Gent said Sinivasan has a controlling interest in a number of companies involved in chemicals, textiles and textile engineering, including PT Polysindon Eka Perkasa, valued at $1.2 billion on the Jakarta Stock Exchange.
